name: Ptr
notes: Runtime signature with attached documentation metadata.

docs.description: The Ptr Lua function returns the handle to a child object.
docs.example: This example prints the data connected to the first child of the selected sequence. It uses the Dump() function.
docs.example_code:
return function()
    -- SelectedSequence() creates a handle to the selected sequence.
    local selectedSequence = SelectedSequence()
    -- Check that a handle was returned - if not then exit function.
    if selectedSequence == nil then
        ErrPrintf("There is no selected sequence.")
        return
    end
    -- Get a handle to the first child object.
    local firstChild = selectedSequence:Ptr(1)
    -- Print some feedback.
    if firstChild ~= nil then
        Printf("=============== START OF DUMP ===============")
        firstChild:Dump()
        Printf("================ END OF DUMP ================")
    else
        ErrPrintf("The object do not have a child object.")
    end
end

name: ToAddr
notes: Runtime signature with attached documentation metadata.

docs.description: The ToAddr Lua object function converts a handle to an address string that can be used in commands.
docs.example: This example returns the address of the first sequence of the selected data pool, prints the address in the Command Line History, and creates a grandMA3 command with a "Go" keyword in front of the address. This command is sent to the grandMA3 command line.
docs.example_code:
return function()
    -- Stores the handle in a variable.
    local mySequence = DataPool().Sequences[1]
    if mySequence ~= nil then
        -- Converts the handle to the address and store in variable.
        local mySequenceAddressName = mySequence:ToAddr(true)
        local mySequenceAddress = mySequence:ToAddr(false)
        -- Print the address to the Command Line History.
        Printf("The named address of the sequence is: " .. mySequenceAddressName)
        Printf("The system address of the sequence is: " .. mySequenceAddress)
        -- Send a 'Go' command with the address appended.
        Cmd("Go %s", mySequenceAddress)
    else
        ErrPrintf("The sequence could not be found")
    end
end

name: Import
notes: Runtime signature with attached documentation metadata.

docs.description: The Import object  Lua function imports an object written in XML format.
docs.example: This example imports the content of an XML file into the selected sequence. The file is called "MySelectedSequence", and it is located at "../gma3_library/datapools/sequences". The file can be created using the example in the Export object function.
docs.example_code:
return function()
    --SelectedSequence() creates a handle to the selected sequence.
    -- The imported object will be merged into this sequence.
    local selectedSequence = SelectedSequence()
    -- Check if there is a selected sequence - if not then exit the function.
    if selectedSequence == nil then
        ErrPrintf("The selected sequence could not be found.")
        return
    end
    --The path is stored in a variable.
    local path = GetPath(Enums.PathType.UserSequences)
    --The actual import function.
    local success = selectedSequence:Import(path, "mySelectedSequence.xml")
    --Print some feedback. 
    if success then
        Printf("The sequence is imported from: " .. path .. GetPathSeparator() .. "mySelectedSequence.xml")
    else
        ErrPrintf("The object could not be imported.")
    end
end

name: Addr

docs.description: The Addr Lua object function converts a handle to an address string that can be used in commands.
docs.example: This example prints different versions of the address to a cue in a sequence:
docs.example_code:
return function()
    -- Creates a cue in sequence 1
    Cmd("Store Sequence 1 Cue 100 /Merge /NoConfirmation")
    --Store a handle to the created cue
    local cueObject = ObjectList("Sequence 1 Cue 100")[1]
    --Print different version of the handle address
    Printf("ToAddr:              " .. cueObject:ToAddr())
    Printf("Addr:                " .. cueObject:Addr())
    Printf("Addr(Parent, false, false): " .. cueObject:Addr(cueObject:Parent(), false, false))
    Printf("Addr(Parent, true, false):  " .. cueObject:Addr(cueObject:Parent(), true, false))
    Printf("Addr(Parent, false, true): " .. cueObject:Addr(cueObject:Parent(), false, true))
    Printf("Addr(Parent, true, true):  " .. cueObject:Addr(cueObject:Parent(), true, true))
end

name: SetFader

docs.description: The SetFader function sets a fader to a specified level. It must be used on an object that has faders.
docs.example: This example changes the selected sequences' Master fader to 100% and the Time fader to 5 seconds and enables the time fader.
docs.example_code:
return function()
    -- SelectedSequence() creates a handle to the selected sequence.
    local selectedSequence = SelectedSequence()
    -- Set the master fader to 100. The FaderMaster is the default token, so it can be omitted.
    selectedSequence:SetFader({value=100.0})
    -- Set the time fader to 5 seconds and enable the fader.
    selectedSequence:SetFader({value=50.0, faderEnabled=1, token="FaderTime"})
end

name: AddrNative
notes: Runtime signature with attached documentation metadata.

docs.description: The AddrNative Lua object function converts a handle to an address string that can be used in commands.
docs.example: This example prints the address of the first sequence:
docs.example_code:
return function()
    -- Stores the handle to the first sequence.
    local mySequence = DataPool().Sequences[1]
    -- Print the native address.
    Printf("The full address is: " .. mySequence:AddrNative())
    -- Stores a handle to the default DataPool.
    local myDataPool = DataPool()
    -- Print the native address to the datapool using the default datapool as a base.
    Printf("The address in the datapool is: " .. mySequence:AddrNative(myDataPool))
    -- Print the native address to the datapool, using the default datapool as a base, with names as strings.
    Printf("The address in the datapool with quotes around the names is: " .. mySequence:AddrNative(myDataPool, true))
end

        ErrPrintf("The property could not be found.")
    end
end

name: HookObjectChange
notes: Runtime signature with attached documentation metadata.

docs.description: The HookObjectChange Lua function automatically calls a function when a grandMA3 object changes.
docs.example: To call a function every time the content of the sequence pool changes, create a plugin with this code:
docs.example_code:
-- Get the handle to this Lua component.
local luaComponentHandle = select(4,...)

function Main()
    -- Get a handle to the sequence pool.
    local hookObject = DataPool().Sequences
    -- Get a handle to this plugin.
    local pluginHandle = luaComponentHandle:Parent()
    -- Create the hook and save the Hook ID.
    SequenceHookId = HookObjectChange(MySequencePoolCallback, hookObject, pluginHandle)
    -- Print the returned Hook ID.
    Printf("HookId: " .. SequenceHookId)
end

-- This function is called when there are changes in the sequence pool.
function MySequencePoolCallback(obj)
    Printf(tostring(obj.name) .. " changed!")
end

return Main

name: CreateMultiPatch
notes: Runtime signature with attached documentation metadata.

docs.description: The CreateMultiPatch Lua function creates a series of multi patch fixtures to a table of fixtures.
docs.example: This example creates two multi patch fixtures to the first fixture (excluding the "Universal" fixture) in the patch.
docs.example_code:
return function()
    -- Enter Patch.
    Cmd("ChangeDestination Root");
    -- Enter the SetupPatch.
    Cmd("ChangeDestination 'ShowData'.'Patch'");

    -- Get the handle for the first fixture in the patch.
    local myFixture = Patch().Stages[1].Fixtures[2]
    -- Add the handle a list element in an table.
    local myFixtureTable = {myFixture}
    -- Add a variable with the amount of multipatch fixtures needed.
    local multiPatchAmount = 2

    -- Count the number of elements in the fixture table and store in a variable.
    local count = 0
    for _ in pairs(myFixtureTable) do
         count = count + 1
    end
    -- Create an unto text string.
    local undoText = string.format("Create %d multipatch fixtures for up to %d fixtures", multiPatchAmount, count)

    -- Create the multipatch fixtures to the each fixture handle in the table and store the returned value.
    local multiPatchAmount = CreateMultiPatch(myFixtureTable, multiPatchAmount, undoText)
    if multiPatchAmount ~= nil then
        Printf(multiPatchAmount .. " multi patch objects was created")
    else
        Printf("An error occured")
    end

    -- Return the command line destination to the root.
    Cmd("ChangeDestination Root")
end

name: GetPresetData
notes: Runtime signature with attached documentation metadata.

docs.description: The GetPresetData Lua function returns a table with the preset data based on the preset handle.
docs.example: This example prints information about the first level table in the preset data and the first level of the first fixture in the preset. It uses dimmer preset 1, which must exist.
docs.example_code:
return function()
    -- Get the handle for the first Dimmer preset.
    local myPreset = DataPool().PresetPools[1][1]
    -- Get the Preset Data of the handle.
    local myPresetData = GetPresetData(myPreset, false, false)
    -- Check if the GetPresetData returns something. 
    if myPresetData == nil then
        ErrPrintf("Dimmer preset 1 does not exist. Please create one and try again.")
        return
    end

    -- Print the myPresetData table.
    for Key, value in pairs(myPresetData) do
      if type(value) == "table" then
        Printf("Key: " .. Key .. " ; Value type is: " .. type(value))
      else
        Printf("Key: " .. Key .. " ; Value type is: " .. type(value) .. " ; Value: " .. value)
      end
    end

    -- Create a table object to hold all the integer keys in the myPresetData table.
    local myIntegerTableKeys = {}
    -- Fill the table.
    for key,_ in pairs(myPresetData) do
        if type(key) == "number" then
            table.insert(myIntegerTableKeys, key)
        end
    end
    -- Sort the table
    table.sort(myIntegerTableKeys)

    -- Print the elements of the fixture with the lowest ui_channel_index in the preset.
    local tableIndex = myIntegerTableKeys[1]
    if tableIndex ~= nil then
        Printf("=============== TABLE CONTENT START - Table Key: " .. tableIndex .." ===============")
        for Key, value in pairs(myPresetData[tableIndex]) do
          if type(value) == "table" then
            Printf("Key: " .. Key .. " ; Value type is: " .. type(value))
          else
            Printf("Key: " .. Key .. " ; Value type is: " .. type(value) .. " ; Value: " .. tostring(value))
          end
        end
        Printf("================ TABLE CONTENT END - Table Key: " .. tableIndex .." ================")
    end
end

    --Print the feedback from the closing action - 1 = Success / 0 = Failure.

        ErrPrintf("The CloseUndo was not successful")

name: Time
notes: Runtime signature with attached documentation metadata.

docs.description: The Time function returns the time (in seconds) the station has been on, as a number (float). It is basically a stopwatch that starts when the grandMA3 application starts. It is not the current time of day or the session online time.
docs.example: This example finds, formats, and prints the time.
docs.example_code:
return function()
    -- Get the current time
    local time = Time()

    --Calculate the different elements
    local days = math.floor(time/86400)
    local hours = math.floor((time % 86400)/3600)
    local minutes = math.floor((time % 3600)/60)
    local seconds = math.floor(time % 60)

    --Print the result
    Printf("The time is %d:%02d:%02d:%02d", days, hours, minutes, seconds)
end

name: CheckDMXCollision
notes: Runtime signature with attached documentation metadata.

docs.description: The CheckDMXCollision Lua function checks if a specific DMX address range is available or already used.
docs.example: This example prints feedback to the DMX collision check based on a DMX address of "1.001" and the DMX mode of the first fixture in the current selection:
docs.example_code:
return function()
    -- Set the DMX universe - range 1-1024.
    local myDMXUniverse = 1
    -- Set the DMX address in the universe - range 1-512.
    local myDMXAddress = 1
    -- Set the optional count for the number of fixtures (break_index channel amount) to check.
    local myCount = 1
    -- Set the optional break_index number for fixtures with multiple breaks. 
    -- Default value is 0 to indicate the first break.
    local myBreakIndex = 0

    -- Creates the string used for the DMX address.
    local startOfRange = string.format("%d.%03d", myDMXUniverse, myDMXAddress)

    -- Check if there is a selection and exit if there isn't.
    if SelectionFirst() == nil then
        Printf("Please make a selection and try again.")
        return
    end
    -- This gets the handle for the first fixture a patched generic Dimmers 8-bit mode.
    local myDmxMode = GetSubfixture(SelectionFirst()).ModeDirect

    if myDmxMode == nil then
        -- Exit the function if the DMX mode returns nil.
       
    else
        -- Do the actual collision check and provide useful feedback.
        if CheckDMXCollision(myDmxMode, startOfRange, myCount, myBreakIndex) then
            Printf("The DMX address " .. startOfRange .. " is available.")
            return
        else
            Printf("The DMX address " .. startOfRange .. " cannot be used as a start address for this patch.")
            return
        end
    end
end

docs.description: The GetTopModal Lua function returns a handle for the modal at the top. Modal is the internal name for pop-ups that interrupt the system's normal operation. A modal blocks other UI elements from being used while it is open.
docs.example: This example uses the Dump() function to show information about the StagePopup selection pop-up.
docs.example_code:
return function()
    -- Open a Modal / Pop-up.
    Cmd('Menu "StagePopup"')
    -- Add a small wait.
    coroutine.yield(0.5)
    -- Get the handle for the modal / pop-up. 
    local modalHandle = GetTopModal()
    -- If there is a handle then dump all information else print en error feedback.
    if modalHandle ~= nil then
        Printf("=============== START OF DUMP ===============")
        modalHandle:Dump()
        Printf("================ END OF DUMP ================")
    else
        ErrPrintf("The Modal UI object could not be found.")
    end
    -- Close the modal / pop-up by pressing the Escape key.
    Keyboard(1,'press','Escape')
    Keyboard(1,'release','Escape')
end

The function returns a "true" boolean value if the addition was a success. The function must be run with the command line in the correct patch destination.
docs.example: This example adds a dimmer fixture with FID and CID 301 and patch address "10.001". It is a requirement that the generic dimmer type is already added to the show, that the ID and patch address are available, and that the stage is called "Stage 1". The example does not perform any check for availability.
docs.example_code:
return function()
    -- Change the command line destination to the root.
    Cmd("ChangeDestination Root")
    -- Enter the "Patch".
    Cmd('ChangeDestination "ShowData"."Patch"')
    -- Enter the fixture location for the "Stage 1" object.
    Cmd('ChangeDestination "Stages"."Stage 1"."Fixtures"')

    -- Create a table.
    local myAddFixtureTable = {}
    -- Set the mode to a 8-bit Dimmer fixture type. 
    myAddFixtureTable.mode = Patch().FixtureTypes.Dimmer.DMXModes["Mode 0"]
    -- Set the amount of fixtures.
    myAddFixtureTable.amount = 1
    -- Set the FID for the fixture.
    myAddFixtureTable.fid = "301"
    -- Set the IdType - it is not needed if the type is "Fixture".
    myAddFixtureTable.idtype = "Channel"
    -- Set the CID - Use only this when the "idtype" is different than Fixture.
    myAddFixtureTable.cid = "301"
    -- Set the name of the fixture.
    myAddFixtureTable.name = "AddedDimmer 301"
    -- Create a patch table with an address.
    myAddFixtureTable.patch = {"10.001"}

    -- Add the fixture to the patch using the table data. Store the result in a local variable.
    local success = AddFixtures(myAddFixtureTable)
    
    -- Provide some feedback.
    if success ~= nil then
        Printf("Fixture " .. myAddFixtureTable.fid .. " is added with patch address " .. myAddFixtureTable.patch[1])
    else
        Printf("AddFixture failed!")
    end
    
    -- Return the command line to the root destination.
    Cmd("ChangeDestination Root")
end

return function()
    --- grandMA3 full-size modules are:
    --- Master Module (MM): "UsbDeviceMA3 2"

        return

    for key,value in pairs(buttonTable) do
        if tostring(value) == "true" then
            Printf("The button with the index " .. key .. " is pressed.")
        end
    end
end

name: CheckFIDCollision
notes: Runtime signature with attached documentation metadata.

docs.description: The CheckFIDCollision Lua function checks if a specific (range of) ID is available or already used. It can be used to check FID and any type of CID by adding a type integer.
docs.example: This example prints feedback to the FID check:
docs.example_code:
return function()
    -- Create a variable with the FID you want to check.
    local myFID = 2001
    -- Create a variable with the number of subsequent ID's to also check.
    local myCount = 10
    -- Create a variable with the IDType you want to check.
    -- Default value is 0. This is the "Fixture" type.
    -- Valid integers are:
    --- 0 = Fixture
    --- 1 = Channel
    --- 2 = Universal
    --- 3 = Houseligths (default name)
    --- 4 = NonDim (default name)
    --- 5 = Media (default name)
    --- 6 = Fog (default name)
    --- 7 = Effect (default name)
    --- 8 = Pyro (default name)
    --- 9 = MArker
    --- 10 = Multipatch
    local myType = 0

    -- Check if the count is more than one.
    if myCount > 1 then
        -- Check if there is a collision and print valid feedback.
        if CheckFIDCollision(myFID, myCount, myType) then
            Printf("The FID " .. myFID .. " to " .. (myFID + myCount) .. " is available.")
            return
        else
            Printf("The FID " .. myFID .. " to " .. (myFID + myCount) .. " gives an FID collision.")
            return
        end
    else
        if CheckFIDCollision(myFID, nil, myType) then
            Printf("The FID " .. myFID .. " is available.")
            return
        else
            Printf("The FID " .. myFID .. " gives an FID collision.")
            return
        end
    end
end

name: Timer

notes: Runtime signature with attached documentation metadata.

data.signature: Timer(function:timer_function, integer:delay_time, integer:max_count[, function:cleanup][, light_userdata:context object]): nothing

docs.description: The Timer Lua function call a different function using a timer. The other function can be called multiple times using the timer interval.
docs.example: This example prints a greeting three times and then calls a clean up function:
docs.example_code:
-- Function that will be called several times.
function TimedFunction()
    -- Check the value of RunAmount and print something.
    if RunAmount 1 then
        Printf("Hello")
    else
        Printf("Hello again")
    end
    -- Add 1 to the RunAmount variable.
    RunAmount = RunAmount + 1
end

-- Cleanup function.
function TimerCleanup()
    Printf("Goodbye")
    -- Delete the RunAmount variable.
    RunAmount = nil
end

-- Function with the Timer call.
function Main()
    -- Set a wait variable.
    local waitSeconds = 1
    -- Set a variable with the number of iterations.
    local iterations = 3
    -- Create a counter variable and set it to 0.
    RunAmount = 0
    -- Call the timer function.
    Timer(TimedFunction, waitSeconds, iterations, TimerCleanup);
end

-- call the main function.
return Main

name: GetPathOverrideFor

docs.description: The GetPathOverrideFor Lua function delivers a string with the path of a grandMA3 folder. The function is relevant when the path should be on a removable drive connected to a console.
docs.example: This example prints the override path of the macro folder on the system monitor. It should be run on a console with a removable drive connected.
docs.example_code:
return function ()
    -- Set a path for the first removable media.
    -- Set the initial value to nil.
    local myBasePath = nil
    -- Itereate the drives and find the first 'Removeable' drive and store the path.
    for _, value in ipairs(Root().Temp.DriveCollect) do
        local driveType = value.drivetype
        if driveType == "Removeable" then
            myBasePath = value.path
            break
        end
    end
    -- If no removeable drive was found, then provide feedback and exit the function.
    if myBasePath == nil then
        ErrPrintf("No removeable drive could be found. Please insert one and try again")
        return
    end

    -- Get the integer for the UserMacros path type.
    local myPathType = Enums.PathType.UserMacros

    -- Gey the string for the path override.
    local myOverridePath = GetPathOverrideFor(myPathType, myBasePath)
    -- Print the returned string.
    Printf("The path is: " .. myOverridePath)
end

return function()

    -- Unblock the station
    SetBlockInput(false)
end

notes: The NotebookLM research treats grandMA2 3.9.60.2 as the terminal software version.

name: lua
notes: grandMA2 plugins use Lua 5.3 in v3.1+; the Lua keyword executes Lua 5.3.

notes: ReloadPlugins restarts the Lua engine and is required after Lua changes.

name: macros
notes: Basic command-line syntax is [Function] [Object].

name: variables
notes: SetVar creates global show variables; SetUserVar creates current-user variables.

name: variables
notes: AddVar/AddUserVar can add numbers and append text; variables must already exist.

name: variables
notes: ListVar shows both global/user/system variables; ListUserVar shows current-user variables.

name: variables
notes: To delete a variable, use SetVar $name = (nothing / empty assignment), not an empty quoted string.

name: macro_input
notes: Parentheses create user-input popups; quoted prompt text is needed when assigning text values.

name: macro_cli
notes: The @ placeholder enables command-line interaction in macros.

name: psr
notes: Partial Show Read imports selected objects from another show and requires leaving an active session.

name: psr
notes: Source and destination show files should be stored in the same software version for PSR.

name: parameters
notes: grandMA2 full-size unlocks 8192 parameters; light/ultra-light/RPU/NPU 4096; a session can reach 65536 parameters.

name: parameters
notes: For console-based sessions, NPU is the parameter-expansion device; grandMA2 onPC is limited to 4096 parameters.

The semicolon separates multiple commands.
Official grandMA3 v2.3 command keyword.
The dot is a separator which is used in fractional digits and hierarchic IDs of objects.
The = [Equal] character is used when assigning a value to an object setting.

name: #[Object]
notes: The #[Object] is used instead of object numbers or names in order to address an object. Using #[Object] makes it unnecessary to update macros or commands if the object was moved or the name of the object was changed.
The $ (dollar sign) character is used to address variables using the command line.
The <<< [GoFastBackward] keyword is a playback keyword which is used to jump to the previous cue in a sequence, without using cue timing.
The >>> [GoFastForward] keyword is a playback keyword which is used to jump to the next cue in a sequence without using cue timing.

syntax: ([Attribute] ["Attribute_Name" or Attribute_Number]) At - [Value] | [Object] ["Object_Name or Object_Number] - [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] [Number]
notes: The - [Minus] keyword is used to remove objects from a list or to indicate negative values.
The * [Asterisk] is a placeholder which is used to substitute any other character or characters in a name.

syntax_rejected.text: Hint: The * [Asterisk] can be positioned anywhere within the name string.

notes: The % [Percent] keyword is a helping keyword that can be used as a scaling operator.

syntax: (Attribute ["Attribute_Name" or Attribute_Number]) At + [Value] | [Function] [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] + ["Object_Name" or Object_Number]
notes: The + [Plus] keyword is a helping keyword that has various functions.

name: Absolute
notes: The Absolute keyword is used to address the absolute layer.

name: Acceleration
notes: The Acceleration keyword is used to set the acceleration curve of a step in the phaser.

name: Action
notes: The Action keyword is used to call functions that do not have a designated keyword.

name: Agenda
notes: The Agenda keyword represents the single agenda events.

name: ActivationGroup
notes: The ActivationGroup keyword represents attributes that are activated together.

name: Align
notes: The Align keyword is a function keyword which is used to toggle through the align modes of the attribute encoders.

name: AlignTransition
notes: The AlignTransition keyword is used to toggle between the align transition modes:

name: Appearance
syntax: Assign Appearance ["Appearance_Name" or Appearance_Number] At [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number]
notes: The Appearance keyword is used to assign an appearance to an object.

syntax: Assign Appearance ["Appearance_Name" or Appearance_Number] At [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number]

name: Assign
syntax: Assign [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] At [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] | Assign Off [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] At [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number]
notes: The Assign keyword is a function which is used to assign objects to other objects.

syntax: Assign [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] At [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number]
Assign Off [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] At [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number]

name: At
syntax: At ([Value_Type]) [Value] | At [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] | [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] At ([Value_Type]) [Value] | [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] At [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] | [Destination] At [Source] (If [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number]) (/Option) | [Function] [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] At [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number]
notes: The At keyword is a function keyword and a helping keyword at once.

name: Attribute
notes: The Attribute keyword is an object keyword which is used to set attributes of a fixture.

name: AutoCreate
syntax: AutoCreate [Source_Object] ["Source_Object_Name" or Source_Object_Number] At [Destination_Object] ["Destination_Object_Name" or Destination_Object_Number] (/Option)
notes: The AutoCreate keyword creates objects depending on predefined source objects. It can, for example, create groups in the fixture types of the patched fixtures.

syntax: AutoCreate [Source_Object] ["Source_Object_Name" or Source_Object_Number] At [Destination_Object] ["Destination_Object_Name" or Destination_Object_Number] (/Option)

name: AutoStore
notes: The AutoStore keyword is used to directly store presets in a fixture type. This can be useful, for example, when you have to use a fixture type in a different show file, and want to save time by creating your own standard set of presets.

name: Bitmap
notes: The Bitmap keyword allows you to use media files such as images or videos, also called bitmap generator objects, and map them to the selection of fixtures.

name: Black
notes: Black is a playback keyword that is used to temporarily override the master level to zero on executing objects.

name: Blind
notes: The Blind keyword is used to suppress the output of the live programmer. It is possible to program without putting the content live. Disabling Blind activates the programmer and the changes made during the mode.

name: Block
syntax: Block (Sequence ["Sequence_Name" or Sequence_Number]) Cue ["Cue_Name" or Cue_Number] (If Fixture ["Fixture_Name" or Fixture_Number] FeatureGroup ["FeatureGroup_Name" or FeatureGroup_Number] or Attribute ["Attribute_Name" or Attribute_Number] EndIf)
notes: Block is a function used to add data and prevent them from tracking. Tracked values are converted to stored values.

syntax: Block (Sequence ["Sequence_Name" or Sequence_Number]) Cue ["Cue_Name" or Cue_Number] (If Fixture ["Fixture_Name" or Fixture_Number] FeatureGroup ["FeatureGroup_Name" or FeatureGroup_Number] or Attribute ["Attribute_Name" or Attribute_Number] EndIf)
examples: Block Cue 5 If Fixture 4 FeatureGroup "Position" EndIf

name: BPM
syntax: At Speed BPM [Value] | Master [Master_Number] At BPM [Value]
notes: The BPM keyword is used to set the speed of a fixture selection or a speed master using the unit BPM.

name: Call
notes: The Call keyword is used to apply an object or its content.

name: CancelSoftwareUpdate
notes: The CancelUpdateSoftware keyword is a function keyword which is used to cancel the running process of sending grandMA3 update files to other grandMA3 devices in the network.

name: Camera
notes: The Camera keyword selects a camera in the camera pool.

name: Capture
notes: The Capture keyword is a command keyword which is used to activate the current output values of specified parameters.

name: ChangeDestination
syntax: ChangeDestination ["Element_Name" or Element_Number] | ChangeDestination Root | ChangeDestination ..
notes: The ChangeDestination keyword is a function keyword used to change the current destination of the command line.

name: Channel
notes: The Channel keyword is an object keyword used to select fixtures of the ID type Channel.

name: ChangeMulticastBase
notes: The ChangeMulticastBase keyword is a function keyword used to change the current address of the Multicas t Base.

name: ChannelFunctionDefault
syntax: ChannelFunctionDefault | Fixture ["Fixture_Name" or Fixture_Number] At ChannelFunctionDefault
notes: The ChannelFunctionDefault keyword is used to set all attributes to the default value of the first channel function.

name: ChannelSet
notes: The ChannelSet keyword is used to take channel sets, such as gobos, actively into the programmer.

name: Chat
notes: The Chat keyword is used to send messages via the world server in chat channels that were already joined. These chat messages are displayed in the message center.

name: ChatJoin
notes: The ChatJoin keyword is used to join a chat channel.

name: ChatLeave
notes: The ChatLeave keyword is used to leave a chat channel.

name: CleanUp
notes: The CleanUp keyword is a command keyword that is used to delete objects that are not used and do not contain references in the show file. For example, you can clean up sequences that are not assigned to an executor.

name: Clear
notes: The Clear keyword is a function keyword which is used to clear the selection, active values, or the programmer.

name: ClearActive
notes: âThe ClearActive keyword is used to deactivate all values in the programmer.

name: ClearAll
notes: The ClearAll function clears the selection and discards all values in the programmer.

name: ClearSelection
notes: The ClearSelection keyword is a function keyword which is used to deselect the selected fixtures.

name: Clone
syntax: Clone [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] At [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] (If [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] /Option) | Clone [Source_Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] At [Destination_Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] (/Option)
notes: Clone replicates data from one fixture or selection to another throughtout the show file. For more information on applying values live in the programmer only, see the At keyword .

syntax: Clone [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] At [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] (If [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] /Option)
Clone [Source_Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] At [Destination_Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] (/Option)

name: CommandDelay
syntax: CommandDelay [CommandDelay_Value] | ([Function]) (Sequence ["Sequence_Name" or Sequence_Number]) Cue ["Cue_Name" or Cue_Number] CommandDelay [CommandDelay_Value]
notes: The CommandDelay sets the delay time when executing commands in a cue.

syntax: ([Function]) (Sequence ["Sequence_Name" or Sequence_Number]) Cue ["Cue_Name" or Cue_Number] CommandDelay [CommandDelay_Value]

name: Collect
notes: The Collect keyword is used to add objects of the same type to a collection. For more information on collection see Collection Keyword .

name: Collection
notes: The Collection keyword is an object keyword used to represent the current collection of objects.

name: Color
notes: The Color keyword is an object keyword which is used, for example, to adjust the color of the color theme to your liking.

name: ColorDefinition
notes: The ColorDefinition keyword is an object keyword which is used, for example, to adjust the color defintion of the color theme to your liking.

name: ColorTheme
notes: ColorTheme is an object keyword which is used, for example, to adjust the color theme.

name: Configuration
syntax: [Function] Configuration ["Configuration_Name or Configuration_Number] At [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number]
notes: A configuration contains a set of different button, key, fader, and encoder functions. It can be assigned to an executor.

syntax: [Function] Configuration ["Configuration_Name or Configuration_Number] At [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number]

name: Console
notes: The Console keyword is an object keyword which is used to address all grandMA3 consoles in the network.

name: Cook
notes: The Cook keyword is a command keyword which is used to concoct recipes of objects without accessing the editor.

name: Copy
syntax: Copy [Object] ["Source_Name" or Source_Number] At ["Destination_Name" or Destination_Number] (/Option) | Copy [Object] ["Source_Name" or Source_Number] (/Option)
notes: The Copy keyword is a function keyword which is used to create copies of an object.

syntax: Copy [Object] ["Source_Name" or Source_Number] At ["Destination_Name" or Destination_Number] (/Option)

name: Cue
syntax: [Function] Cue ["Cue_Name" or Cue_Number] | [Function] Sequence ["Sequence_Name" or Sequence_Number] Cue ["Cue_Name" or Cue_Number] ([Setting] ["Setting_Value"] (/Option) | Assign [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] At (Sequence ["Sequence_Name" or Sequence_Number]) Cue ["Cue_Name" or Cue_Number]
notes: Important: Cue is the only object type that accepts numerical IDs as decimal fractions. The ID which is allowed for cues ranges from 0.001 to 9999.999. In all other objects, a dot indicates the ID of a parent or a child object.

syntax: [Function] Sequence ["Sequence_Name" or Sequence_Number] Cue ["Cue_Name" or Cue_Number] ([Setting] ["Setting_Value"] (/Option)
Assign [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] At (Sequence ["Sequence_Name" or Sequence_Number]) Cue ["Cue_Name" or Cue_Number]

name: CopyCrashLog
notes: CopyCrashLog is a function keyword that is used to copy crash logs into the crash logs folder in the gma3_library folder on any device.

name: CueAbsolute
notes: CueAbsolute is a layer keyword. It is used to change the selected layer to the CueAbsolute layer. This layer can show information in, for instance, the fixture sheet. The layer shows the cue ID number for each parameter that has an absolute value from the active cues.

name: CueDelay
syntax: (Cue ["Cue_Name" or Cue_Number]) CueDelay [CueDelay_Time] | (Cue ["Cue_Name" or Cue_Number]) CueDelay [CueInDelay_Time]/[CueOutDelay_Time]
notes: CueDelay can set both the indelay and the outdelay time of a cue. To do so, use a /. See examples further down.

name: CueFade
syntax: (Cue ["Cue_Name" or Cue_Number]) CueFade [CueFade_Time] | (Cue ["Cue_Name" or Cue_Number]) CueFade [CueInFade_Time]/[CueOutFade_Time]
notes: CueFade can set both the infade and the outfade time of a cue. To do so, use a /. See examples further down.

name: CueInDelay
notes: CueInDelay sets the delay time of a cue.

name: CueInFade
notes: CueInFade sets the infade time of a cue.

name: CueOutDelay
notes: CueOutDelay sets the outdelay time of a cue.

name: CueOutFade
notes: CueOutFade sets the outfade time of a cue.

name: CueRelative
notes: CueRelative is a layer keyword. It is used to change the selected layer to the CueRelative layer. This layer can show information in, for instance, the fixture sheet. The layer shows the cue ID number for each parameter that has a relative value from the active cues.

name: CueUpdate
notes: CueUpdate keyword is an object keyword which addresses all cues that can be updated.

name: CurrentEnvironment
notes: The CurrentEnvironment keyword addresses the currently selected environment of the current user - Live or Preview.

name: CurrentUser
notes: CurrentUser represents the user that is currently logged in.

name: CurrentUserProfile
notes: The CurrentUserProfile keyword represents the profile of the current user.

name: Cut
notes: The Cut keyword is a function keyword used to specify the source objects for a two-step action.

syntax_rejected.text: The object is temporarily stored for later use as source object for the following Paste command.
For more information on Cut & Paste see the Paste Keyword .

name: DataPool
notes: The DataPool keyword is used to address a data pool or objects outside the data pool you are currently in.

name: Deceleration
notes: The Deceleration keyword is used to set the deceleration curve of a step in the phaser.

name: Deactivate
notes: The Deactivate keyword deactivates active data in the programmer. Values will not be stored when storing cues or presets as values are subject to store settings.

name: Decimal8
notes: The Decimal8 keyword is used to set the values of a fixture selection using the 8bit decimal notation.

name: Decimal16
notes: The Decimal16 keyword is used to set the values of a fixture selection using the 16bit hexadecimal notation.

name: Decimal24
notes: The Decimal24 keyword is used to set the values of a fixture selection using the 24bit decimal notation.

name: Default
syntax: Default | Fixture ["Fixture_Name" or Fixture_Number] At Default ( FeatureGroup ["FeatureGroup_Name" or FeatureGroup_Number]) | Store Default (/Option)
notes: The Default keyword is used to reset the attributes of your fixture selection to default values. If there is no attribute list, all attributes of the selected fixtures will be set to their default values.

syntax: Fixture ["Fixture_Name" or Fixture_Number] At Default ( FeatureGroup ["FeatureGroup_Name" or FeatureGroup_Number])

name: Delay
notes: Delay sets the delay time of an object.

name: DeleteGlobalVariable
notes: The DeleteGlobalVariable keyword is used to delete global variables in a show.

name: Delete
notes: The Delete keyword is a function keyword which is used to remove data in a show file.

name: DeleteOtherVersion
notes: The DeleteOtherVersion keyword is a function keyword that is used to delete the installation files of the software versions in a grandMA3 device.

name: DeleteUserVariable
notes: The DeleteUserVariable keyword is used to delete user-specific variables.

name: Disconnect
notes: The Disconnect keyword disconnects the station from session. Contrary to Dismiss, the Disconnect keyword only disables the network of the station and does not reset the name of session and location of the device. Disconnect only works in devices that take part in the same session.

name: Dismiss
notes: The Dismiss keyword is used to throw stations out of your session.

syntax_rejected.text: Find the device number in the Network menu :
To show the devices, unfold the device type. Along with other information, each device displays number, IP address, and name.

name: Display
notes: Display is an object keyword which is used to manage the displays.

name: DMXAddress
notes: The DMXAddress keyword is used to access DMX addresses directly using an absolute numbering method.

name: DMXLayer
notes: DMXLayer is a layer keyword. It is used to change the selected layer to the DMXLayer. This layer can show information in, for instance, the fixture sheet.

name: DMXReadout
notes: The DMXReadout keyword is used to set the readout of DMX values in the user profile. It affects the display of values when editing a fixture type or the normal value in the user profile.

name: DMXUniverse
syntax: [Function] DMXUniverse ["DMXUniverse_Name" or DMXUniverse_Number] | DMXUniverse ["DMXUniverse_Name" or DMXUniverse_Number] At ([Readout]) [Value]
notes: The DMXUniverse keyword is used to access DMX universes or all DMX channels of a universe.

name: DoubleSpeed
notes: The DoubleSpeed keyword is a playback keyword which is used to change the speed of the speed masters, presets, or sequences to double the speed.

name: Down
notes: The Down keyword is a function keyword which is used to address the subfixture within the main fixture.

name: DumpLog
notes: DumpLog is a function keyword that is used to deposit the output of the system monitor in form of a text file in case you should experience any inconsistencies or errors in the software. Hence, use this keyword if you are prompted by the tech support. Regardless of the location the files are stored to â internally or to a USB drive â the path is always gma3_library.

name: Drive
syntax: [Function] Drive ["Drive_Name" or Drive_Number] | [Command] If Drive ["Drive_Name" or Drive_Number]
notes: The Drive keyword is used to address physical drives, for instance, USB flash drives and the internal hard drive.

name: DropOwnership
notes: The DropOwnership keyword is used when a user wants to edit an object that is currently owned by a different user. DropOwnership sends a request to release the ownership of an object.

name: Echo
notes: The Echo keyword is used to display feedback in the windows Command Line History and the System Monitor .

name: Edit
notes: Edit is a function keyword which is used to modify values.

name: EditSetting
notes: EditSetting is a function keyword which is used to modify the settings of an object.

name: Eject
notes: The Eject keyword is used to eject a USB flash drive.

name: EditRecipe
syntax: EditRecipe ([Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] or ["Recipe_Name" or Recipe_Number])
notes: The EditRecipe is a function keyword that enables the recipe editor.

syntax: EditRecipe ([Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] or ["Recipe_Name" or Recipe_Number])

name: Effect
notes: The Effect keyword is an object keyword which is used to call fixtures of the ID type Effect in the programmer.

name: EncoderBank
notes: The EncoderBank keyword is an object keyword which addresses encoder banks.

name: EncoderBar
notes: Official grandMA3 v2.3 command keyword.

name: EndIf
syntax: [Function] If [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] EndIf [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number]
notes: EndIf is a helping keyword that indicates the end of an If statement.

syntax: [Function] If [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] EndIf [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number]

name: Environment
notes: The Environment keyword is used to grant access to the two environments of the user profile - normal and preview. Each environment has its own programmer, selection, At filter and other.

name: Exchange
syntax: Exchange [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] At [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number]
notes: The Exchange keyword is a function keyword used to swap places.

syntax: Exchange [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] At [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number]

name: Executor
syntax: Executor [Executor_ID] | Select Page [Page_ID] Executor [ Executor_ ID] | Set Executor [Executor_ID] [Setting] = [Setting_Option ]
notes: The Executor keyword is an object keyword used as a control handle for other objects.

name: Export
notes: Export is a function keyword which is used to save objects from the current show file as a smaller file.

name: Extension
notes: The Extension keyword is an object keyword which is used to address all extensions in the network.

name: Extract
notes: The Extract keyword is a command keyword used to call the values of presets without references.

name: Fade
notes: The Fade keyword is a helping keyword which is used to indicate fade times.

name: FaderCrossFade
syntax: [Function] FaderCrossFade At [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] | FaderCrossFade [Object] ["Object_Name or Object_Number] At [Value]
notes: The FaderCrossFade keyword represents the crossfade function of a sequence.

name: FaderCrossFadeA
syntax: [Function] FaderCrossFadeA At [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] | FaderCrossFadeA [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] At [Value]
notes: The FaderCrossFadeA keyword represents the crossfade A function of a sequence.

name: FaderCrossFadeB
syntax: [Function] FaderCrossFadeB At ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] | FaderCrossFadeB [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] At [Value]
notes: The FaderCrossFadeB keyword represents the crossfade B function of a sequence.

name: FaderMaster
syntax: Assign FaderMaster At [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] | FaderMaster [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] At [Value] (Fade [Time])
notes: The FaderMaster keyword applies the Master function to a number of objects such as executors, sequences, groups, masters, and other.

syntax_rejected.text: Only sequences and presets can move the master using a fade time. Other objects snap to the value.

name: FaderRate
syntax: Assign FaderRate At [Object] ["Object_Name " or Object_Number] | FaderRate [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] At [Value]
notes: The FaderRate keyword applies the Rate function to a number of objects such as executors, sequences, groups, masters, presets, and other.

name: FaderSpeed
syntax: Assign FaderSpeed At [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] | FaderSpeed [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] At [Speed_Readout] [Speed_Value]
notes: The FaderSpeed keyword applies the Speed function to a number of objects such as executors, sequences, groups, masters, and other.

name: FaderTime
syntax: Assign FaderTime At [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] | FaderTime [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] At [Value]
notes: The FaderTime keyword applies the Time function to a number of objects such as executors, sequences, groups, masters, and other. It is used to overwrite the stored cue part times by setting a time value and activating the time function.

name: FaderTemp
syntax: Assign FaderTemp At [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] | FaderTemp [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] At [Value]
notes: The FaderTemp keyword applies the Temp function to a number of objects such as executors, sequences, groups, masters, and other.

name: FeatureGroup
notes: The FeatureGroup keyword is used to address feature groups.

name: Filter
notes: The Filter keyword is used to call a filter. It represents an attribute and a layer filter.

name: Fix
syntax: Fix (On or Off) Executor [Executor_Number] | Fix (On or Off) Page ["Page_Name" or Page_Number].[Executor_Number]
notes: Fix is a function keyword which is used to latch executors on a page. The executors that are latched will always be displayed, even if you change the page.

syntax: Fix (On or Off) Page ["Page_Name" or Page_Number].[Executor_Number]

name: Fixture
syntax: Fixture ["Fixture_Name" or Fixture_Number] | Fixture ["Fixture_Name" or Fixture_Number].["SubFixture_Name" or SubFixture_Number]
notes: The Fixture keyword is used as an object keyword to access fixtures that have a fixture ID.

name: FixtureClass
notes: FixtureClass is an object keyword which addresses the fixture classes of a show file.

name: FastSync
notes: The FastSync keyword is a playback keyword that is used to determine the starting point of the phaser. The first step of the phaser is immediately started.

name: FixtureLayer
notes: FixtureLayer is an object keyword which addresses the layers of fixtures in a show file.

name: FixtureType
notes: FixtureType is an object keyword which addresses the fixture types of a show file.

name: Flash
notes: The Flash keyword is a playback keyword which is used to temporarily overwrite master level in order to set it to full on executing objects without using times.

name: Flip
notes: The Flip keyword is used to access the different pan/tilt combinations that direct a moving head in the same direction.

name: Fog
notes: The Fog keyword is an object keyword which is used to call fixtures of the ID type Fog in the programmer.

name: Freeze
notes: Freeze is a function keyword which is used to change the priority of the programmer.

name: Full
notes: Full is a function keyword which is used to set the dimmer values to 100 %.

name: Gel
notes: The keyword Gel provides the opportunity to edit or apply swatch book colors using the command line.

name: Generator
syntax: (Attribute ["Attribute_Name" or Attribute_Number]) At Generator ["Generator_Name" or Generator_Number]
notes: The Generator keyword is an object keyword which is used to address the Generator pool objects.

syntax: (Attribute ["Attribute_Name" or Attribute_Number]) At Generator ["Generator_Name" or Generator_Number]

name: GetGlobalVariable
notes: The GetGlobalVariable keyword is used to display global variables along with their values in the command line history.

name: GetUserVariable
notes: The GetUserVariable keyword is used to display user-specific variables along with their values in the command line history.

name: Go+
notes: The Go+ keyword is a playback keyword and it operates as a start signal for commands to be executed.

name: Go-
notes: The Go- keyword is a playback keyword that is used to activate the previous cue.

name: Goto
notes: Goto is a function keyword that is used to jump in a list using the original cue timing of the cue where the values were initially stored. Setting fade times using the Goto keyword overrides the original cue timing. For more information s ee Relevant Playback Commands .

name: Grid
notes: The Grid keyword is used to set the grid cursor or span a grid area in the selection grid window. After the cursor is set, it is possible to arrange fixtures in the selection grid window. To position fixtures with a z-axis in the selection window, use the Grid keyword.

name: GridPosition
notes: GridPosition is a layer keyword which represents the xyz grid coordinates of fixtures at a time as values were set in attributes. It is used to change the selected layer to GridPosition. This layer can show information in, for instance, the fixture sheet.

name: GridStore
notes: GridStore transfers grid positions of subfixtures to fixture types.

name: GoboImage
notes: The keyword GoboImage is an object keyword. It is used to manage images of gobos using the command line.

name: Group
notes: The Group keyword is an object type that contains a certain selection of fixtures in a specific order along with xyz-coordinates used in the Selection window .

name: HalfSpeed
notes: The HalfSpeed keyword is a playback keyword which is used to change the speed of the speed masters, presets, or sequences to half the speed.

name: Help
notes: Help is a function keyword which is used to open the Help pop-up for you to search for topics or to use the context sensitive help.

name: HelpLua
notes: HelpLua is a function keyword which is used to export a list of all grandMA Lua functions.

name: Hex8
notes: The Hex8 keyword is used to set the values of a fixture selection using the 8bit hexadecimal notation.

name: Hex16
notes: The Hex16 keyword is used to set the values of a fixture selection using the 16bit hexadecimal notation.

name: HelpKeyword
notes: HelpKeyword is a function keyword which is used to list all grandMA3 keywords.

name: Hex24
notes: The Hex24 keyword is used to set the values of a fixture selection using the 24bit hexadecimal notation.

name: Highlight
notes: The Highlight keyword is a playback keyword that is used to apply the defined highlight values on fixtures that are selected.

name: Hold
notes: The Hold keyword is a special value that prevents an MIB action while the dimmer is closed. Hold can only be applied to a dimmer attribute and is equivalent to a value of 0.

name: Houselights
notes: The Houselights keyword is an object keyword which is used to call fixtures of the ID type Houselights in the programmer.

name: Hz
syntax: At Speed Hz [Value] | Master [Master_Number] At Hz [Value]
notes: The Hz (Hertz) keyword is used to set the speed of a fixture selection or a speed master using the unit hertz.

name: If
syntax: ([Function] [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number]) If [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] | Clone [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] At [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] If [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number]
notes: The If keyword is a function keyword which is used to deselect fixtures in a selection.

syntax: Clone [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] At [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number] If [Object] ["Object_Name" or Object_Number]

name: IfActive
notes: IfActive is a function keyword that selects fixtures with active values in the programmer.

name: IfProgrammer
notes: IfProgrammer is a function keyword that selects fixtures that contain values in the programmer.

name: IfOutput
notes: IfOutput is a function keyword that selects fixtures based on their current output. This function works with presets and sequences only.

name: Image
notes: The keyword Image is an object keyword. It is used to manage images using the command line.

name: Import
syntax: Import [Object] Library "File Name.xml" (If Drive [Drive_Number]) (At ["Object_Name" or Object_Number]) (/Option) ("Option_Value")
notes: Import is a function keyword that incorporates small portions of exported show file data, available as XML files, into the current show file.

syntax: Import [Object] Library "File Name.xml" (If Drive [Drive_Number]) (At ["Object_Name" or Object_Number]) (/Option) ("Option_Value")

name: Index

syntax_rejected.text: The supported types are:
True False Null Impulse Timetag
Hint: When using the OSC types True, False, Nil/Null, Impulse and Timetag it is not necessary to enter a value.
Hint: Several values can be sent at once when separated by commas.
Important: When addressing an executor, a page must be specified as well.
Instead of using page and executor numbers, it is also possible to address them by name.
When addressing executor keys, a value of 0 will be interpreted as not pressed. Values greater 0 will be interpreted as button press.
If a prefix is specified for an OSCData entry, then this very prefix will be added to the sent string when using the OSCSend command.

Hint: The supported OSC types to control faders, executor knobs, and buttons are: Integer32, Float32, True, False and Nil/Null. A True will be interpreted as 1, while a False will be interpreted as 0.

name: Preset
syntax: Preset [ID] | Preset [Preset-type].[ID] | Preset "Name" | Assign Preset [ID] / [Parameter] = [Parameter Value]
notes: With the Preset keyword you can:

syntax: PresetType [PresetType Number] | PresetType "PresetType Name" | PresetType [PresetType Number] . [Feature Number] | PresetType [PresetType Number] . [Feature Number] . [Attribute Number] | [Function Keyword] PresetType [PresetType Number] . [Feature Number]
