Store If PresetType Position If Selection

name: Preview
syntax: Preview [cue-object] / [option] = [option value] | Preview [part-object] | Preview Next | Preview Previous
notes: The Preview keyword creates a preview of the programmed output without having an actual DMX output.

examples: Preview Cue 5 Load cue 5, part 2 of the selected executor in the preview editor.
Preview Cue 5 Part 2 Load current cue of executor 3 in the preview editor.

name: PreviewEdit
notes: The PreviewEdit toggles between the live programmer and the blind preview editor.

name: PreviewExecutor
notes: Requirement: A sequence loaded in the preview editor.

examples: Go PreviewExecutor Requirement: Selected sequence in the preview editor. Store cue 5 in the preview sequence.

name: Previous
notes: The Previous keyword has multiple functions.

name: PrevRow
notes: If MAtricksInterleave is on, PrevRow reduce the Single Y value by one. If Single Y was at 0, the last Single Y value will be used. For more information, see MAtricks .

name: Profile
syntax: [Function] Profile [DMX Profile ID].[DMX Profile Point ID] | Assign Profile [DMX Profile ID].[DMX Profile Point ID] /[Parameter]=[Parameter Value]
notes: The Profile keyword is an object keyword to access DMX profiles and DMX profiles points. For more information, see DMX profiles .

syntax: [Function] Profile [DMX Profile ID].[DMX Profile Point ID]
Assign Profile [DMX Profile ID].[DMX Profile Point ID] /[Parameter]=[Parameter Value]

name: Protocol
syntax: [Function] Protocol [Network Protocol ID] . [Row ID] | Assign Protocol [Network Protocol ID] / [Parameter] = [Parameter Value] | Assign Protocol [Network Protocol ID] . [Row ID] / [Parameter] = [Parameter Value]
notes: The Protocol keyword is an object keyword to access the network protocols.

syntax: Assign Protocol [Network Protocol ID] . [Row ID] / [Parameter] = [Parameter Value]
examples: Assign Protocol 4 /outactive=on Send grandMA2 universe 10 to Art-Net universe 9. Important: Art-Net universe 0 is the first Art-Net universe.

name: PSR
notes: Requirement: The partial show read is prepared.

examples: PSR /? The PSR keyword has the following options. Option Short Cut Description merge m Adds to existing content. overwrite o Replaces existing content. Examples Partial show read on sequence 1.
PSR Sequence 1 Partial show read on sequence 1, if channel 1 through 3 are used.

name: PSRList
notes: The PSRList keyword lists all available and changed objects of the show file which can be inserted. The PSRList keyword displays the same as the partial show read pop-up tree. For more information, see Partial Show Read (PSR) .

name: PSRPrepare
notes: PSRPrepare prepares a showfile for PartialShowRead.

name: Rate
notes: The Rate keyword is a function to adjust the Rate of an executor.

examples: Assign Rate Exec 6 Set the rate for a sequence on executor 1 and 5 to 2.

name: Rate1
notes: The Rate1 keyword resets the rate to 1:1.

name: RdmAutomatch
notes: Requirements: - MA Fixture is not matched - MA Fixture and RDM Fixture have the same DMX address - MA Fixture Type has no or the same RDMFixtureType ID as the RDM Fixture - MA Fixture Type has the same DMX footprint as the RDM Fixture - All Subfixtures of the MA Fixture are in the current World and Filter

examples: RdmAutomatch To automatch the fixtures used in group 1, type in the command line:
RdmAutomatch Group 1 To automatch only the fixtures used in group 1 and also used in sequence 2, type in the command line:

name: RdmAutopatch
notes: Requirements: - MA Fixture is matched - MA Fixture is patched - MA Fixture and RDM Fixture have the same universe

examples: RdmAutopatch To autopatch the fixtures used in group 1, type in the command line:
RdmAutopatch Group 1 To autopatch only the fixtures used in group 1 and also used in sequence 2, type in the command line:

name: RdmFixtureType
notes: The RdmFixtureType is an object keyword to access Rdm fixtures with a Rdm fixture type ID.

examples: RdmAutomatch RdmFixtureType 1 To unmatch RDM fixture type 1, type in the command line:

name: RdmInfo
notes: The RdmInfo keyword opens the RDM info pop-up with the actual RDM information to the entered fixture or channel.

examples: RDMInfo Fixture 3 The RDM Info pop-up opens. RDM Info pop-up To open the RDM Info pop-up for fixture 3 on screen 3: 1. Type in the command line:

name: RdmList
notes: The RdmList keyword generates a list of the received RDM data. The list is displayed in the command line feedback window.

examples: RdmList Fixture 3 To get the RDM list of fixture 3 in the command line feedback window and as a .txt file called RDM Fixture 3 in the temp folder, type in the command line:

name: RdmSetParameter
notes: With the RdmSetParameter keyword you can set RDM parameters by using the command line.

examples: RdmSetParameter dmx_start_address 3 / UID = 43500F019FCB To invert the display of a RDM device for the selected fixture, type in the command line:

name: RdmSetpatch
notes: With the RdmSetPatch keyword you set the DMX address of a RDM fixture by using the command line.

examples: RdmSetPatch 25 To set the fifth multipatch fixture of the current fixture selection to the DMX address 25, type in the command line:
RdmSetPatch 25 / multipatch = 5 To set the DMX address of the fixture with the UID 43500F019FCB to 25, type in the command line:

name: RdmUnmatch
notes: The RdmUnmatch keyword unmatches previous matched RDM devices in the show file. If no object is given, the current selection will be used.

examples: RdmUnmatch To unmatch the fixtures used in group 1, type in the command line:
RdmUnmatch Group 1 To unmatch the fixtures used in group 1 and in sequence 2, type in the command line:

name: Reboot
notes: The Reboot keyword, shutdown the station and boot it up again.

examples: Reboot /? The reboot keyword has the following options. Option Option Shortcut Description save s Saves the show file before reboot. nosave ns Do not saves the show file before reboot. noconfirm nc Suppress reboot confirmation pop-up. force f Forces a reboot. Examples Reboot the current console.
Reboot Reboot a station with the IP address 192.168.0.32 in the network.

name: Record
notes: The Record keyword records real time actions as timecodes or macros. For more information, see record a timecode show or record a macro .

examples: Record Timecode 1 Stop all running timecode records from the timecode pools.

Record Timecode Start to record command line actions as macro 5. The macro record icon is visible in the command line, if in the message center options for macro status yes selected is. The keys Learn and Macro are flashing.
Record Macro 5 Stops all running macro records from the macro pools.
Record Macro Record the receiving timecode as trig time by calling the cue, if the selected trigger is timecode . The timecode record icon is visible in the command line.
Record Executor 1 Turn off the timecode executor record from executor 1.

name: Release
notes: The Release keyword enters release values in the programmer for attributes by the given object list, filtered by the current selection.

examples: Release Selection Enter release values in the programmer for pan and tilt attributes of the fixture selection.
Release PresetType "position" Enter release values in the programmer for the running effect 4 .

name: ReloadPlugins
notes: The ReloadPlugins keyword restarts the LUA engine.

name: Remote
syntax: [Function] Remote [Remote Input Type ID] . [ID] | Assign Remote [Remote Input Type ID] . [ID] / [Parameter] = [Parameter Value] | If you store a remote input type, the IDs needs to be in an order and beginning from 1.
notes: The Remote keyword is an object keyword to access the remote input types.

syntax: Assign Remote [Remote Input Type ID] . [ID] / [Parameter] = [Parameter Value]
If you store a remote input type, the IDs needs to be in an order and beginning from 1.
examples: Store Remote 3.1 Assign an existing remote a DMX address, a remote type and a command.

name: RemoteCommand
notes: The RemoteCommand keyword executes commands at a specific console.

examples: RemoteCommand 192.168.0.4 "View 3" Start macro 4 only on a specific console.

name: Remove
notes: The Remove keyword enters remove values in the programmer for attributes by the given object list, filtered by the current selection.

examples: Remove Selection Enter remove values for pan and tilt in all layers for the current selection, or for all fixtures if no selection.
Remove PresetType "position" Enter remove values for dimmer attribute for fixture 1.

name: RemoveIndividuals
notes: RemoveIndividuals is a command used to delete individual values of effects and effect lines.

examples: RemoveIndividuals Effect 1 Thru 10 Removes the individual values in effect 1 through 10.

name: Replace
syntax: Replace [ search for objects] With [ replace with objects] ( If [ search in objects] )
notes: The replace keyword replaces object and values. For more information, see search and replace .

syntax: Replace [ search for objects] With [ replace with objects] ( If [ search in objects] )
examples: Replace Attribute "Pan" At - 270 Thru 270 With - 260 Thru 280 Subtract 10 % from all dimmer values in all cues from sequences 3.
Replace Attribute "Dim" At 0 Thru 100 With 0 Thru 90 If Sequence 3 Replace the individual fade time of 5 by 10 for attribute tilt.

Replace Attribute "Tilt" Fade 5 with Fade 10 Hint: If you would like to replace two fixtures with each other, use a third fixture. See the examples below this box. Replace fixtures with each other in three steps: Replace fixture 2 with 3.
Replace Fixture 2 with 3 Replace fixture 1 with 2.
Replace Fixture 1 with 2 Replace fixture 3 with 1.
Replace Fixture 3 with 1 Delete a specific fixture from everywhere where it is linked to.
Replace Attribute "Pan" At - 270 Thru 270 With - 260 Thru 280
Replace Attribute "Dim" At 0 Thru 100 With 0 Thru 90 If Sequence 3

name: ResetDmxSelection
notes: The ResetDmxSelection keyword clears the selection in the DMX tester .

name: ResetGuid
notes: ResetGuid resets the identifiers that are unique in every object. This command is mainly used with the Partial Show Read.

name: Restart
notes: The Restart keyword restarts the application. This is the same as close the program and open it again.

examples: Restart Restart the application of the console with the IP address 192.168.0.32 in the network.

name: Root
notes: The Root keyword access the root in the object tree.

examples: ChangeDest Root DMX_Protocols.Art-Net Export all live setup layers from the grandMA2 onPC to the folder C:\ProgramData\MA Lighting Technologies\grandma\gma2_V_3.1\fixture_layers.

name: Rotate3D
notes: The Rotate3D keyword rotates 3D objects in the Stage View .

name: SaveShow
notes: The SaveShow keyword saves the show on the selected drive. For more information, see SelectDrive Keyword .

syntax_rejected.text: The option noconfirm suppress the save show confirmation pop-up.

name: Screen
notes: The Screen keyword represents the screens.

examples: Delete Screen 2 Hint: Another way to clear the screen is, press and hold the key and tap Clear Screen . Assigns mask 5 to the third window of the second screen.

name: Search
syntax: Search [ search for objects] ( At [search values] ) If [ search in objects]
notes: The Search Keyword searches for objects and values in the show. For more information see search and replace .

syntax: Search [ search for objects] ( At [search values] ) If [ search in objects]

name: SearchResult
syntax: SearchResult | SelFix SearchResult | Search [object-list] If SearchResult
notes: The SearchResult keyword opens the world search result after an executed search command. The search result world includes only the fixtures or channels from the last search command.

examples: SearchResult Select only the fixtures from the last search result.
SelFix SearchResult Search in the last search result for fixtures with the attribute green at 20.
Search Fixture Thru Attribute "G" At 20 If SearchResult

name: Select
syntax: Select [Executor-object] | Select Layout [ID] | Select Mask [ID] | Select Filter [ID] | Select TimecodeSlot [ID] | Select Timecode [ID] | Select Timer [ID] | Select Camera [ID]
notes: The Select keyword, selects objects as default objects.

examples: Select Executor 5 Select layout 2 in the layout view. Requirement: Layout Selection is set to Link Selected.

name: SelectDrive
notes: The SelectDrive keyword select the drive in the Backup Menu , for the following functions:

examples: SelectDrive Load demoshow "demo dimmer and more".

name: Selection
notes: The Selection keyword represent the current channels and fixtures selection in the programmer.

name: SelFix
notes: The SelFix keyword creates fixture selections in the programmer.

examples: SelFix Executor 1 Select all fixtures stored in preset 1.
SelFix Preset 1 Select all fixtures used in effect 3.

name: Semicolon ; Character
notes: The semicolon separates multiple commands.

name: Sequence
notes: The default function of the sequence keyword is SelFix .

examples: Sequence 5 Block all cues of sequence 5.

name: SetHostname
notes: The SetHostname keyword, sets the station name of the console.

name: SetIP
notes: The SetIP keyword changes the IP address of the Ethernet interfaces of the console or station.

examples: SetIP eth0 192.168.0.5 Sets the IP address of the first Ethernet interface.
SetIP eth0 /DHCP Activates DHCP client which takes over the IP address automatically from the server.
SetIP eth1 2.0.0.10 /mask=255.0.0.0 Sets IP address and network mask for the second Ethernet interface.

name: SetNetworkSpeed
notes: The SetNetworkSpeed keyword, changes the port speed of the first network adapter of grandMA2 consoles and MA NPU.

name: Setup
notes: The Setup keyword opens or closes the setup menu.

name: SetUserVar
syntax: SetUserVar $variablename = numericvalue | SetUserVar $variablename = "text" | SetUserVar $variablename = ("text") | SetUserVar $variablename = nothing
notes: The SetUserVar keyword sets user profile specific variables. For more information, see Macros - Use Variables .

name: SetVar
syntax: SetVar $variablename = numericvalue | SetVar $variablename = "text" | SetVar $variablename = ("text") | SetVar $variablename = nothing
notes: The SetVar keyword sets global show variables. Every user profile can use these variables. For more information, see Macros - Use Variables .

name: ShuffleSelection
notes: The ShuffleSelection keyword mix-up the order of the selected fixture or channel.

name: ShuffleValues
notes: The ShuffleValues keyword mix-up the values of the selected fixtures or channels.

examples: ShuffleValues Mix up the pan and tilt values of the fixture selection.

name: Shutdown
notes: The shutdown keyword switches the grandMA2 console off or close the grandMA2 onPC.

examples: Shutdown /? The shutdown keyword has the following options. Option Option Shortcut Description save s Saves the show file. nosave ns Do not saves the show file. noconfirm nc Suppress shutdown confirmation pop-up. force f Forces a shutdown. Examples 1. Switch station off, by using the IP address.
Shutdown 192.168.0.10 2. Switch station off, by using the host ID of the network.

name: <<< [GoFastBack]
notes: Official grandMA2 v3.9 keyword.

syntax_rejected.text: The time used by this function may be adjusted via the GoFast property found in Setup -> Show -> Playback + MIB Timing.

name: >>> [GoFastForward]
notes: Official grandMA2 v3.9 keyword.

syntax_rejected.text: The time used by this function may be adjusted via the GoFast property found under Setup -> Show -> Playback + MIB Timing.

name: Slash / Character
notes: The slash separates entered object properties or parameter options.

examples: Copy /? 2. Press Please . The copy options are displayed in the command line feedback window. Figure 1: Command line feedback window - copy options To change the parameters for cue 5 on the selected executor: 1. Type in the command line:

name: SnapPercent
notes: Important: To use the SnapPercent it is necessary that attributes of the fixture types must have Snap On. Go to the Patch & Fixture Schedule I Fixture Types . Select a fixture type and click Edit , in the column Snap select On.

examples: Store Cue 1 SnapPercent 4 Assign a snap percent to an existing cue.

name: Solo
notes: The Solo keyword forces zero values for intensity output for attributes of all unselected fixtures or channels. Only the selected fixtures or channels will have intensity output for attributes.

name: SpecialMaster
notes: Specialmaster is an object type that holds predefined objects for global control.

name: Speed
notes: With the Speed keyword, you assign faders the function speed. Speed adjust the effect speed in the cues and the speed of a chasers for the selected executor.

examples: Assign Speed Exec 28 Requirement: A sequence or a chaser is assigned to the executor 3. Sets speed of the sequence or chaser to 120.

name: Square Brackets [ ] Character
notes: Square brackets [ ] are used in macros. For more information see macros .

name: StepFade
notes: With the StepFade keyword, you assign executors as a step fader. A step fader controls the fade time between the steps of a chaser.

examples: Assign StepFade Exec 28 Set the stepfade to 50 % on executor 3.

name: StepInFade
notes: The StepInFade keyword assigns executors as a step in fader. A step in fader controls the step in time of each step of a chaser.

examples: Assign StepInFade Exec 28 Set the step in fade level to 50 % on executor 3.

name: StepOutFade
notes: With the StepOutFade keyword, you assign executors as a step out fader. A step out fader controls the step out time of each step of a chaser.

examples: Assign StepOutFade Exec 28 Set the step out fader level to 50 % on executor 3.

name: Stomp
notes: The Stomp keyword applies values and stops running effects. Stomp will be applied only if an effect is running. If no effect is running, stomp can not be applied.

examples: Stomp 75 Move the current fixture selection to preset "drummer" and stop the current running circle effect.
Stomp Preset "drummer" Select fixture 2, set its dimmer to zero and stop the current running dimmer effects.

name: Store
notes: The store keyword, stores functions in the show file.

examples: Store 7 2. Store dimmer preset 3 with all attributes and keep the values active in the programmer. For more information, see Store Presets .
Store Preset 1.3 /presetfilter=false /ka 3. Store the programmer values as cue 1 through cue 10 and cue 20 through cue 30.

name: StoreLook
notes: StoreLook stores all dimmer values from all fixtures in the show.

name: Surface
notes: The Surface keyword, loads a created surface form the Wing & Monitor Setup .

name: Swop
notes: The Swop keyword temporary overrides the master level of executors to full and set all other master levels to zero.

examples: Swop /? The keyword Swop has the same options as the keyword Goto. For further information see keyword Goto . Examples Override master level of executor 1 to full and all other master levels to zero.
Swop Executor 1 Returns the master level to the master fader position and turns the executor off.

name: SwopGo
notes: The SwopGo keyword temporary overrides the master level of executors to full and all other master levels to zero, and goes to the next cue.

name: SwopOn
notes: The SwopOn keyword temporary overrides the master level of executors to full and all other master levels to zero.

examples: SwopOn /? The keyword SwopOn has the exact same options as the keyword Goto. For further information see keyword Goto . Example 1. Override master level of executor 1 to full and all other master levels to zero.
SwopOn Executor 1 2. Returns the master level to the master fader position. The executor stays on after releasing the executor button.

name: SyncEffects
notes: The SyncEffects keyword starts all running effects synchronous.

name: TakeControl
notes: TakeControl is a keyword used if multiple users are in a session.

name: Telnet
notes: Important: The telnet receiver needs to read the commands without a telnet login. If the telnet receiver asks for a login, the command can not be processed.

name: Temp
syntax: Temp [Object-list] / [Option] = [Option Value] | Temp On [Object-list] / [Option] = [Option Value] | Temp Off [Object-list] / [Option] = [Option Value]
notes: The Temp keyword turns an executor on, as long as you hold the executor button. The Temp keyword follows cue timing, off timing and the position of the master fader from the executor.

examples: Temp On Executor 1 To turn executor 1 temporary off, type in the command line:

name: TempFader
notes: The TempFader keyword, is a function that crossfades the cue on when pulled up, and crossfades the cue off when pulled down.

examples: Assign TempFader Exec 28 Set the temp fader to 50 % for the selected executor.

name: Thru
notes: The Thru keyword reference a range of objects / values. If the start or end is not defined, it will be used the first or last available object / values.

examples: Fixture 3 Thru 6 2. Select all fixture from the beginning through 10.
Fixture Thru 10 3. Delete all cues, beginning with cue 3, from the selected executor.
Delete Cue 3 Thru 4. Select all fixtures. Press Thru (= Fixture Thru).
Fixture Thru 5. Turn off all executor from the current page.
Off Thru 6. Start executors from 4.2 to 5.9.

name: Timecode
notes: The Timecode keyword, select the timecode by default.

examples: Store Timecode 2 Record executor action for timecode show 2.
Record Timecode 2 Pool Object Record Timecode Play timecode show 2.
Go Timecode 2 Pool Object Go Timecode Rewind timecode show 2.
Top Timecode 2 Label timecode show 2 in the timecode pool. The Enter Name for Timecode pop-up opens.
Label Timecode 2 Enter Name for Timecode pop-up Assign timecode show 1 the timecode slot 3.

name: TimecodeSlot
notes: TimecodeSlot is an object type representing the 8 different possible timecode streams.

name: Timer
notes: With the Timer keyword you can edit, start, pause, restart, switch off, select, lock, unlock, and assign timers.

examples: Edit Timer 4 Edit the timer Countdown Assign a countdown time of 20 seconds to the existing timer 4.

name: ToFull
notes: The ToFull keyword sets the masterlevel of objects to 100 %.

examples: ToFull Executor 1 Sets the grandmaster to full.
ToFull SpecialMaster 2.1 Sets the fader of executor 1 with cue mode assert to full.

name: Toggle
notes: The Toggle keyword acts as an on or off keyword, depending of the on/off-status of the object or function/mode it is applied to. If object or function/mode is on, it turns it off. If object or function/mode is off, it turns it on.

examples: Toggle /? The keyword Toggle has the exact same options as the keyword Goto. For further information see the keyword Goto . Examples To turn the running executor 4 off by using the toggle keyword, type in the command line:
Toggle Executor 4 To turn the running sequence 1 off by using the toggle keyword, type in the command line:

name: Tools
notes: The Tools keyword opens or closes the tools menu.

name: Top
notes: The Top keyword jumps to the beginning of the cue list or sets the timecode marker at the beginning of the timecode show.

examples: Top Executor 5 Go to the top of the cue list on executor 5 in 3 seconds.

name: ToZero
notes: The ToZero keyword sets the masterlevel of objects to zero.

examples: ToZero Executor 1 Sets the grandmaster to zero.
ToZero SpecialMaster 2.1 Sets the fader of executor 1 with cue mode assert to zero.

name: Unblock
notes: The unblock keyword convert blocked values in cues (displayed white) into tracking values (displayed magenta).

examples: Unblock Unblock all values from the current cue. The selected executor is on.
Unblock Unblock all values from feature position, fixture 1 in cue 3.
Unblock Cue 3 If Fixture 1 If Feature "Position" Unblock all default values from sequence 1.
Unblock Cue 3 If Fixture 1 If Feature "Position"

name: Unlock
notes: With the unlock keyword, you can unlock previous locked objects.

examples: Unlock Cue 3 2. Unlock world 3 to edit the world.

name: Unpark
notes: With the Unpark keyword, you can unpark previous parked DMX channels.

examples: Unpark DMX 1.1 Thru 1.10 2. Unpark all fixtures and channels.
Unpark DmxUnivers Thru 3. Unpark PresetType Dimmer, of the current fixture selection.

name: Up
notes: The Up keyword scrolls one page up in focused window. It is the same as press the Up key on the console. See Up Key .

name: Update
notes: The update keyword, updates functions in its source objects.

examples: Update 2. Update cue 4 with values that originates from cue 4, as cue only.
Update Cue 4 /originalcontent /cueonly 3. Update color preset 2 with global values, keep them active in the programmer, and without confirmation pop-up. For more information, see Update Presets .

name: UpdateFirmware
notes: Important: The update firmware process can take up to 60 seconds. To double-check if the update firmware process is still running, use the Version keyword . If the update process is still running, the version keyword will display it. If not, the version keyword function is as usual. You can also use the system monitor window, Create Basic Window -> System -> System Monitor .

name: UpdateSoftware
notes: Requirement: An inserted USB stick with a .update file for the appropriate device or program in the root directory. Download the latest software on www.malighting.com.

name: UpdateThumbnails
notes: The UpdateThumbnails keyword updates the thumbnails of the media servers.

syntax_rejected.text: The row ID is the row in the window CITP Network Configuration. For more information see Thumbnail exchange .

name: User
notes: The User keyword displays user details in the command line feedback window.

examples: List User 1 List all user details.

name: UserProfile
notes: The keyword UserProfile displays the user profiles in the command line feedback.

examples: List UserProfile 1 Hint: User profiles can be limited to a specific world. There are three commands that generate the same result: Assigns the user profile 2 to world 1.

name: Value
notes: With the value keyword you can:

examples: Search Value 50 Replace value 50 at channel 1 through 10 with value 60.
Replace Channel 1 Thru 10 Value 50 With 60 Change to the value layer.

name: Version
notes: The version keyword gives you access to version details of the console or software in the commandline feedback window.

name: View
notes: The view keyword calls views on a screen.

examples: View 5 /screen = 2 Store the content of screen 2, 3, and 4 at view object 5.
Store View 5 /screen = 234 Assign view 2 the name Stage Extern.

name: ViewButton
notes: The ViewButton keyword calls the assigned function on the view button . The call function works only if the assigned object supports a call.

examples: Delete ViewButton 4 Label the assigned view button 5 at view page 2.
Label ViewButton 2.5 "Layout" Store a view at key X1.

name: ViewPage
notes: The ViewPage keyword calls the view pages. There are 11 view pages available. This is the same as press and hold the and a V-Key.

name: VPU pixel mapper view
notes: Official grandMA2 v3.9 keyword.

name: WebRemoteProgOnly
notes: The WebRemoteProgOnly keyword, selects in the web remote fixture sheet the option Prg Only (= Programmer Only).

name: With
notes: The With keyword is necessary for the replace function.

examples: Replace Attribute "Pan" At - 270 Thru 270 With - 260 Thru 280 2. Replace dimmer value 50 by dimmer value 55 in the programmer, in all sequences, and cues.

Replace PresetType 1 At 50 With 55 3. Replace dimmer value 50 by dimmer value 55 only in the programmer. Information: This command structure works only, if you type the command by using the keyboard. If you type the command by using the command keys, the At key will interrupt the replace command.
Replace Attribute "Pan" At - 270 Thru 270 With - 260 Thru 280

name: World
notes: The world keyword call worlds along with its filter, and limit the access to the parameters in the word. World 1 is fixed by default and includes all parameters (fixtures and attributes) in the show.

name: Zero
notes: The keyword Zero sets the intensity of the dimmer to zero:

examples: Zero Sets the intensity of fixture 1 trough 10 to zero.
Fixture 1 Thru 10 Zero Sets the master of executor 1 to zero.

name: preset_cli_vs_lua_object_addressing_semantics
notes: Do not conflate grandMA2 CLI Preset syntax with Lua getobj.handle object addressing. Official MA2 3.9 command syntax supports `Preset [Preset-type].[ID]` and `Preset [ID]`. Thus `Preset 1.1` is CLI notation for preset type 1, preset ID 1; the first component is the preset type, not an arbitrary object namespace. Runtime testing separately showed that getobj.handle() does not uniformly resolve the same CLI forms: Preset 1.1/2.1/3.1 returned nil while Preset 4.1 resolved. Bare `Preset 1`, `Preset 2`, `Preset 3`, `Preset 4` resolved in this runtime to objects reporting numbers 4.1, 4.2, 4.3, 4.4 respectively. Therefore bare-ID resolver behavior is context-sensitive and must not be interpreted as preset-type addressing.

data.reasoning_rule: Use official CLI syntax for command generation. Treat gma.show.getobj.handle() addressing as a separate runtime contract and verify the returned object before relying on it.

name: preset_type_and_id_addressing_rule
